job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many people believe that clear, sparkling water from a river or well is always safe to drink, but this is a dangerous myth. Even if water looks clean, it can contain invisible germs that cause serious diseases. Similarly, some think that pouring cooking oil down the sink is harmless because it remains a liquid. In reality, oil hardens in pipes, blocking them and causing major drainage issues. We must also be careful about what we flush. Some people believe that flushing old medicines is safe because they are meant to heal, but these chemicals actually disrupt the biological treatment processes in wastewater plants. Furthermore, many students confuse the terms sewage and sewerage. Sewage refers to the actual wastewater containing organic and inorganic impurities, while sewerage is the vast network of pipes that transports this waste to treatment facilities. Finally, we must stop viewing sludge as useless trash. During the treatment process, sludge is collected and processed to produce biogas or organic manure, which is highly beneficial for soil. By understanding these facts, we can practice better housekeeping and protect our environment from unnecessary pollution.

items.evidence: In reality, oil hardens in pipes, blocking them and causing major drainage issues.
items.q: Why does pouring leftover cooking oil into a sink cause drainage problems?
options: It sets hard inside the pipes
It stays liquid and flows away easily
It kills the germs inside the pipes
It mixes with sewage and turns to sludge
items.explain: Oil hardens in the pipes and blocks them, which causes major drainage issues.

wrong.why: thinks oil is harmless because it is a liquid
invents an effect that is not in the passage

items.evidence: Some people believe that flushing old medicines is safe because they are meant to heal, but these chemicals actually disrupt the biological treatment processes in wastewater plants.
items.q: Meena flushes her old tablets down the toilet. What problem can this cause?
options: They upset the plant's treatment process
They cure the water and help treatment
They harden and block the sewer pipes
They turn the sludge into useless mud
items.explain: Medicine chemicals disrupt the biological treatment processes in wastewater plants, even though they are meant to heal.

wrong.why: thinks medicines are safe because they heal
picks the oil problem from a nearby sentence

items.evidence: Sewage refers to the actual wastewater containing organic and inorganic impurities, while sewerage is the vast network of pipes that transports this waste to treatment facilities.
items.q: A town lays new underground lines to move dirty water to a plant. What is it improving?
options: The sewerage, a network of pipes
The sewage, a network of pipes
The sludge, a store of solid waste
The sewerage, the impurities in the water
items.explain: Sewerage is the network of pipes that carries waste; sewage is the wastewater itself.

wrong.why: thinks sewage and sewerage mean the same
picks another waste term from the passage

items.evidence: During the treatment process, sludge is collected and processed to produce biogas or organic manure, which is highly beneficial for soil.
items.q: A town plant collects sludge. What is the best way to use it?
options: Process it into gas and manure for soil
Dump it away as useless mud
Add it to water to make it clear
Pour it into wells to make water safe
items.explain: Sludge is processed into biogas or organic manure, which is highly beneficial for soil.

wrong.why: thinks added substances make water clear
thinks clear water is always safe
